title: Farik Command
description: A request for the daemon to change something. Shaped like an event: command names what is asked and body carries that command's arguments. The pairing of the two is checked by the reader, farik_protocol::command::command_from_value. A command carries no actor: who asked is the session the command arrived on, and the step that turns a command into an event takes the actor from there rather than from the caller's word for it.

commandBodyWire.title: Command Body Wire
commandBodyWire.description: Every body shape a command carries. The branches have distinct required properties and none accepts an unknown one, so a body matches exactly one; contract_lock, contract_unlock, and task_integrate share taskIdBody for that reason. Which one a command must carry is decided by command, in the reader.

contract.description: A task contract. This schema says only that it is an object: one schema never references another, and the contract's rules, the repeated-id ones among them, belong to farik_core::contract::validate_contract, which the reader calls.

taskTransitionBody.title: Task Transition Body
taskTransitionBody.description: The human moves a task (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2) from any status but escalated. reason is recorded on the move; from blocked it is also the blocker's resolution, and into escalated it is the escalation's words.

humanAcceptBody.title: Human Accept Body
humanAcceptBody.description: The human approves a contract awaiting approval, or accepts a result that waits for them (docs/SPEC.md sections 5.4 and 5.16). An epic's result needs a message, which the reader's caller holds it to.

escalationResolveBody.title: Escalation Resolve Body
escalationResolveBody.description: The human resolves an escalation (docs/SPEC.md section 5.7) by moving the task to a status, with a message the next session about it is given. extra_tries grants that many more attempts, counting the one the resolve starts; only an iterations escalation takes it (ADR 0024).

humanSendBackBody.title: Human Send Back Body
humanSendBackBody.description: The human sends a contract awaiting approval back to refining, or a result that waits for them back to its assignee as a rejection (ADR 0024). message is required; failed_criteria may be empty, and is required so that this body matches no other branch.

questionAnswerBody.title: Question Answer Body
questionAnswerBody.description: The human answers a question an agent asked (docs/SPEC.md section 5.7): question_id is the sequence number of its question.asked.

taskIdBody.title: Task Id Body
taskIdBody.description: The body of a command that names one task and nothing else: contract_lock, contract_unlock, and task_integrate.

agentUpdateBody.title: Agent Update Body
agentUpdateBody.description: The human changes an agent's status (docs/SPEC.md F1). Only the status in phase 3; phase 5's team builder widens it.

sessionStopBody.title: Session Stop Body
sessionStopBody.description: The human stops a running session (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2).

sprintStartBody.title: Sprint Start Body
sprintStartBody.description: The human starts a sprint (docs/SPEC.md sections 3 and 5.5): what it may spend, or null for no budget of its own (ADR 0015). budget_usd is required so that this body matches no other branch.

messagePostBody.title: Message Post Body
messagePostBody.description: The human says something in the team's channel (docs/SPEC.md 5.9). Whether text is blank or too long is the handler's to say, with the rule's own words.

chatMessagePostBody.title: Chat Message Post Body
chatMessagePostBody.description: The human says something in their one-to-one chat with the agent agent_id (docs/SPEC.md 4.3; ADR 0026). There is no author: Farik writes human. Whether the agent exists and is not retired, and whether text is blank or longer than 4,000 code points, is the handler's to say, with the rule's own words.

connectorConnectBody.title: Connector Connect Body
connectorConnectBody.description: Gives the agent agent the custom MCP server server, an mcp_servers entry as team.schema.json shapes it with source custom, or replaces the one of its name (docs/SPEC.md 6.7; ADR 0030). Its keys were already kept on this machine, beside spec_sha256, by whoever sends this, so no value is here: the entry holds key names and header templates only. The handler holds the entry to validate_team, and spec_sha256 to the entry's own hash, then writes the team file and appends connector.connected.

issuer.description: Who signed the agent in, when the connector is signed in to rather than given keys; recorded on connector.connected. The grant itself is kept by whoever sends this, never here.

connectorDisconnectBody.title: Connector Disconnect Body
connectorDisconnectBody.description: Takes the custom MCP server named server away from the agent agent: the team file loses its entry and connector.disconnected is appended. Its keys are deleted by whoever sends this.

toolDecisionBody.title: Tool Decision Body
toolDecisionBody.description: The human allows (tool_approve) or refuses (tool_refuse) one connector call an agent asked about (docs/SPEC.md 5.7; ADR 0031): approval is the sequence number of its tool_approval.requested, and note is what the human says to the agent, absent when they say nothing. Refused unknown_approval when approval names no tool_approval.requested, and approval_decided when it was already allowed or refused. tool_approval.granted or tool_approval.refused is appended with the request's task on its envelope. tool_approve and tool_refuse share this body.

marketingPlanDecideBody.title: Marketing Plan Decide Body
marketingPlanDecideBody.description: The owner approves (decision approve) or sends back (decision return) the marketing plan plan, MP-<n> (docs/SPEC.md 6.5; ADR 0042). note is what the owner says to the agent: required for return, where it is the reason and Farik refuses it blank as marketing_plan_reason_needed, and optional for approve. Only the owner decides, under ask and auto alike: the command arrives on POST /command behind the daemon's token or the browser's command behind its cookie, never from an agent's session. Refused unknown_marketing_plan when plan names none, marketing_plan_decided when it was decided before, and marketing_plan_expired when approving one whose ends_on is past. marketing_plan.approved or marketing_plan.returned is appended with the proposing task on its envelope; an approval also ends every approved plan the new one replaces.

marketingPlanEndBody.title: Marketing Plan End Body
marketingPlanEndBody.description: The owner ends the approved marketing plan plan, MP-<n>, at any time (docs/SPEC.md 6.5; ADR 0042); note says why, when they say. Refused unknown_marketing_plan when plan names none, marketing_plan_not_approved when it was never approved, and marketing_plan_ended when it has ended already. marketing_plan.ended { by_owner } is appended.

socialPostStopBody.title: Social Post Stop Body
socialPostStopBody.description: The owner stops post post, which is going out or is with Buffer (docs/SPEC.md 6.5; ADR 0042): a scheduled post not yet with Buffer records social_post.stopped { by owner }; one Farik has given to Buffer is first deleted from Buffer by Farik's own delete_post, and only when Buffer takes it back is social_post.stopped { by owner, taken_back } recorded. Refused unknown_post when post names none; post_not_going_out for a post that was requested, stopped, missed or failed; post_being_handed_over while Farik is giving it to Buffer, to be tried again in a minute; post_already_out once its time has passed; post_not_taken_back when Buffer would not delete it, with nothing recorded. Only the owner stops a post: the command arrives behind the daemon's token or the browser's cookie, never from an agent's session.

socialPostDecideBody.title: Social Post Decide Body
socialPostDecideBody.description: The owner allows (decision post) or does not allow (decision dont_post) post post, which the Marketing Specialist wrote outside the marketing plan (docs/SPEC.md 6.5; ADR 0042). Allowed, it is recorded as social_post.scheduled { approved_by owner } with the request's task and no agent, and Farik hands it to Buffer an hour before its time, or at once when that hour has passed. Not allowed, social_post.stopped { by declined } is recorded with note, the owner's words, which the agent reads as the owner's own. Refused unknown_post when post names none, post_decided when it was decided before, and post_in_the_past when its time has passed, or is within five minutes for one to allow, since Farik can no longer hand it to Buffer. Only the owner decides, under ask and auto alike.

siteDecideBody.title: Site Decide Body
siteDecideBody.description: The owner allows (allow true) or does not allow (allow false) the site the Procurement Specialist asked to read in request, the sequence number of its site.requested (docs/SPEC.md 6.10; ADR 0039). note is what the owner says to the agent, whichever they decide, at most 600 characters. Allowed, site.approved { host, request, note } is recorded with the request's task and no agent, and so is one for every other request still waiting for the same site, each on its own task; not allowed, site.declined { request, host, note } is recorded for this request alone. Refused unknown_site_request when request names no site.requested, and site_request_decided when it was decided before. Only the owner decides, under ask and auto alike: the command arrives on POST /command behind the daemon's token or the browser's command behind its cookie, never from an agent's session.

siteAddBody.title: Site Add Body
siteAddBody.description: The owner allows a site no agent asked for, or turns one of Farik's back on (docs/SPEC.md 6.10; ADR 0039). site is trimmed, has https:// put before it only when it holds no ://, and is then taken as the site its address names, a host and its www. twin being one: site.approved { host } is recorded with no task, and every request waiting for the site is allowed too. Refused site_invalid for a site Farik cannot open (an address that is not https, a port, a user name, an IP address, a name with no dot), and site_already_allowed for one that is approved.

siteRemoveBody.title: Site Remove Body
siteRemoveBody.description: The owner takes a site away from the Procurement Specialist, whether they allowed it or it is one of Farik's, which this turns off (docs/SPEC.md 6.10; ADR 0039). host is normalised as siteAddBody's site is: site.removed { host } is recorded with no task. Refused site_invalid for a host Farik cannot open, and site_not_allowed for one that is not approved now.

skillLevel.description: Whose skill: the team's (.farik/skills/<name>/) or one agent's (.farik/agents/<agent>/skills/<name>/). With agent, the agent is named in agent; with team there is no agent. The reader refuses both mismatches at /body/agent.

skillSaveBody.title: Skill Save Body
skillSaveBody.description: Adds the skill whose folder is files to level, or replaces the one of its name (docs/SPEC.md 6.7; ADR 0034). files maps each path in the folder to its text, SKILL.md among them; the name is the one in SKILL.md's frontmatter. The handler holds it to check_skill and the counts, writes the folder, then the pin in the team file, then appends skill.added or skill.changed. A name Farik ships is refused skill_name_taken unless replace_shipped is true. The refusals are skill_* codes, agent_unknown and skill_limit_reached.

skillRemoveBody.title: Skill Remove Body
skillRemoveBody.description: Removes the skill name of level: its folder, its pin, and appends skill.removed (docs/SPEC.md 6.7; ADR 0034). A skill whose folder is already gone is unpinned all the same. Refused skill_unknown for a name not pinned there.

skillConfirmBody.title: Skill Confirm Body
skillConfirmBody.description: Confirms on this computer the skill name of level as its folder is now, which the person read as the folder hashing to sha256 (docs/SPEC.md 6.7; ADR 0034). Refused skill_hash_mismatch unless the folder's skill_sha256 is sha256, and with whatever check_skill refuses; the pin is rewritten to that hash when it differs, then skill.confirmed is appended.

emptyBody.title: Empty Body
emptyBody.description: The body of a command that carries nothing: run_stop, sprint_end, team_pause, and team_resume.

commandReply.title: Command Reply
commandReply.description: What the daemon's POST /command answers once the token passes (docs/SPEC.md section 8.2): what the command did, as one sentence and the sequence numbers of the events it appended, or why it did nothing. A reply is what leaves a process, so it has a schema as a command does; farik_protocol::command::reply_from_value reads it against this definition.

kind.description: invalid: the command cannot be handled as given, a schema refusal among them; refused: it cannot be done to what it names as things stand; not_found: what it names is not there; failed: the store, a file, git, or the orchestrator failed.

taskStatus.title: Task Status
taskStatus.description: Where a contract is in the lifecycle of docs/SPEC.md section 5.2, the contract schema's own list.
